project.name: Norn
project.summary: Norn runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex or any command-line agent) on your own computer and keeps long pieces of work going without you, handing each agent off to a fresh session before its memory gets too big. It checks every branch for leftovers before it can merge, watches the instruction files agents read, and asks you only what it cannot decide, through a local dashboard and phone notifications. It is plain Node with no npm packages, plus two small Rust helpers.

nodes.label: Command line (engine/bin/norn.mjs)
nodes.summary: The `norn` command: the one place records are written, and the way people, the timetable and the agents themselves start, stop, queue and merge work.

nodes.label: Dashboard
nodes.summary: The local web dashboard (on this computer only, or your phone over your own private network) where you chat with the controller, answer questions, approve work and watch runs, spending and findings.

nodes.label: Dashboard server and /api router (server.mjs)
nodes.summary: One node:http server; serve() is a hand-rolled router: every GET/POST /api/... route (~84) is a line there, reading the selected project's records, runs and transcripts and writing through the records; it also streams the live run feeds.
nodes.details: Floorplan does not recognize this router, so the scan finds no endpoints: the page -> server connection is the explicit edge "GET/POST /api/*" in docs/architecture.json.

nodes.label: Pages (engine/dash/pages)
nodes.summary: The dashboard's pages (Inbox, Lanes, Runs, Slop, Spend, Context, Roadmap, Ledger, Docs, Settings) and the actions their buttons take, with their look.

nodes.label: Shared page parts (cells, cards, widgets)
nodes.summary: Shared pieces every page is built from: the frame and menu, cards, tables, diffs, the page switcher, word explanations and the home screen.

nodes.label: SloppaChoppa art (engine/dash/norn)
nodes.summary: Draws and animates the pixel-art orc who presents the leftover findings, with his colours.

nodes.label: Engine
nodes.summary: Everything the command line and dashboard share: the records, running and handing off agents, merging, usage limits and the quality checks.

nodes.label: Records, policy and views (records, ledger, policy, digest)
nodes.summary: Keeps the append-only record of every question, decision, instruction and check-in, the project and machine settings, the roadmap and the summaries built from them.

nodes.label: Lanes, runs and the tick (runs, supervisor, tick)
nodes.summary: Runs the check-in on each tick, queues and starts runs per lane, watches each run until it ends, resumes hand-offs in a fresh session and checks an agent's claim that it is done.

nodes.label: Launching agents (executors, launchargs, scope, mail)
nodes.summary: Decides which agent program and model a run uses, checks sign-in and limits before it starts, keeps it inside its brief's files, measures its context size and passes it messages.

nodes.label: Agent adapters (harness/)
nodes.summary: One adapter per kind of agent program (Claude Code, Codex, any other command-line agent, and a fake one for testing) that builds its command and reads its output.

nodes.label: Merge queue and landing (mergeq, mergeland, collide, gate)
nodes.summary: Lines finished branches up one at a time, runs the test command, spots lanes touching the same files, and opens a pull request on GitHub for the owner to approve.

nodes.label: SloppaChoppa (slop/)
nodes.summary: Checks a branch's changes for leftovers (conflict markers, stray logs, unused imports, a committed `.only`) and sends the findings back to the agent before it may merge.

nodes.label: Instruction, guard and drift checks
nodes.summary: Reads the instruction files agents load every turn for bloat, repeats and outdated names, reviews changes, and runs the read-only fixer whose changes the owner approves.

nodes.label: Sync and multi-machine (sync, synccut, claims)
nodes.summary: Multi-home sync: each home publishes its shared logs to branch home/<id> of the ledger remote and fetches the others' (sync), the one-time cut of a state dir into a home (synccut), work and merge-leader claims on the shared claims branch (claims, claimsref), and Settings > Sync's worker thread (syncwork).

nodes.label: Code index and map (codecli, codeindex, codemap)
nodes.summary: `norn code history` (a git-only per-file index) and `norn code map` (this Floorplan map, drawn from the pinned tool in tools/floorplan) behind the dashboard's Code page.

nodes.label: Usage, cost and limits (usage, cost, usageguard)
nodes.summary: Counts tokens and cost per run and model, forecasts when queued work hits the plan's limits, and refuses runs past the hourly or weekly caps.

nodes.label: Test runner (testrun, testcache)
nodes.summary: Runs a project's tests for the agents on a clean folder, reuses results already passed for the same content, and enforces the time budget.

nodes.label: Setup, chat, notify and remote
nodes.summary: Adopts a new repository, runs the controller chat, sends notices to your phone, pairs phones with the dashboard and offers Norn's commands to AI assistants.

nodes.label: OS scheduler setup (sched/)
nodes.summary: Sets up the operating system's own timetable on Windows, Linux or Mac so the check-in runs automatically every few minutes.

nodes.label: Check-in replay (eval/)
nodes.summary: Replays past check-ins from a copy of the records on a different agent or model and reports where its decisions differ.

nodes.label: Tool-call hook (engine/hook-rs, Rust)
nodes.summary: A tiny program the agent runs before and after every tool call; it answers 'nothing to do' on its own and only wakes the full command line when there is mail or a call to check.

nodes.label: Code graph indexer (engine/code-rs, Rust)
nodes.summary: Parses the project's JavaScript, Python and Rust files and records which file imports which, keyed by commit, so other parts can ask what a change reaches.

nodes.label: Coding agents
nodes.summary: The command-line coding agents Norn starts for each run, such as Claude Code and Codex, running on this computer.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.summary: Where finished lanes become pull requests and where test results on them are watched.

nodes.label: Phone notifications
nodes.summary: ntfy and Pushover, which carry Norn's notices to the owner's phone when they opt in.

edges.label: every few minutes
edges.description: The operating system's timetable runs `norn tick`, which starts the next check-in.

edges.label: starts agent
edges.description: The supervisor launches the chosen agent program for a run and watches it until it exits.

edges.label: each tool call
edges.description: Claude runs started by Norn call the fast check before and after every tool call.

edges.label: mail / scope check
edges.description: When there is mail or a call it cannot clear, the fast check hands over to `norn mail check` or `norn scope check`.

edges.label: opens pull request
edges.description: Merging a lane pushes its branch and opens a pull request through the gh command; it never pushes main.

edges.label: GET/POST /api/*
edges.description: Every page loads its data with fetch(/api/<name>?project=P) and posts its actions to /api/...; the routes are the if (route === ...) lines of serve() in engine/dash/server.mjs.

edges.label: reads / writes records
edges.description: The /api routes read the project state (records, runs, transcripts) and every button press goes through the records.

edges.label: claims pass per tick
edges.description: Each tick renews this home's lane and merge-leader claims and fences runs whose claim was not confirmed (tick.mjs claimsPass).

annotations.note: The single biggest file: every `norn` command, and the only writer of the records.
The /api router: serve() holds every dashboard endpoint as an if (route === ...) line; Floorplan cannot see them, so the map shows the router as the GET/POST /api/* edge.

flows.title: A lane's work, start to merge

steps.note: The computer's timetable runs the check-in every few minutes.
The check-in looks at the records, then fills the run queue within the usage limits.
A supervisor starts the run and keeps its heartbeat, usage and hand-off going.
The coding agent does the work in the lane's own copy of the repo.
On every tool call the fast check passes on mail and keeps the agent inside its brief.
The agent reports `norn done`; Norn checks the tree, scope and tests itself.
The branch is checked for leftovers, tested, and lined up to merge.
A pull request is opened for the owner to approve.
A notice tells the owner something needs them.
The Inbox shows the question with its options and a recommended answer.
The chosen answer is sent to the dashboard server.
It is written as a ruling in the records, and the waiting run picks it up.

tour.title: What Norn is
tour.note: Norn keeps coding agents working on your projects while you are away. Everything goes through the `norn` command, which writes every decision to a permanent record.

tour.title: The dashboard
tour.note: Where you chat with the controller, answer questions, approve work and see runs, spending and findings, on your computer or phone.

tour.title: Keeping work going
tour.note: Every few minutes a check-in starts queued runs, watches them, and resumes long work in a fresh session from the agent's hand-off.

tour.title: The agents doing the work
tour.note: Norn starts Claude Code, Codex or another command-line agent for each run, each in its own copy of the repo.

tour.title: Guarding quality
tour.note: Before a branch can merge, SloppaChoppa checks it for leftovers and sends them back to the agent to fix.

tour.title: Getting work into main
tour.note: Finished branches are tested one at a time and turned into GitHub pull requests for you to approve.

tour.title: Your inbox
tour.note: The page you'll use most: every question waiting for you, with a recommended answer.
